title: How the U.S. Doomsday Plane Works
fullNarrative:
(bright music) - The Boeing VC-25 is perhaps the most
iconic plane in the world, and it is of course the aircraft that the US president most
often uses while traveling, giving it the call sign Air Force One. (bright music continues) But there is also a lesser known aircraft that is just as vital
to the president, one that hopefully would
never need to be used. This is the Boeing E-4B, better
known as the Doomsday Plane, and its nickname is not
exaggerated, as the plane was made for nuclear war. (energetic music) A plane built for the end of the world, designed to survive when
everything else fails, able to command an
entire war from the sky, and packed with technology
the public almost never sees. And for this video, I
digitally reconstructed and mapped out the inside
(video whooshes) of the aircraft to understand how the Doomsday Plane actually works. (bright music) The Doomsday Plane exists to
solve one very unique problem. What if the United States
hit by a nuclear attack? This hypothetical scenario
became very real during the 1950s and '60s when the Cold War
tension was at its peak. Both the US and the Soviet Union were amassing massive
stockpiles of nuclear warheads, and both nations were
proving that they can strike the other nation, with the United States stationing nuclear missiles in Europe, and during the Cuban missile crisis, the Soviet Union placing
their missiles in Cuba. During this time, the
United States established a complex system of protocols for how it would actually carry out a nuclear strike against an enemy, because in order to
authorize a nuclear strike, there is one person, and one
person only who can do it, and that is, of course, the president. The president's call with orders to strike would then be processed for the US Strategic Air Command, which is located at Offutt
Air Force Base in Nebraska. (bright music continues) This location was chosen because
it is roughly in the middle of the country and sits
well beyond the range of hostile missiles or
nuclear armed bombers. From this command center,
orders are carried out to complete the strike
using any capability of the US Nuclear Triad, because the US has three main
ways in which it can launch a nuclear strike, from land
using intercontinental missiles, from the sea using nuclear submarines, or from the air using bombers. (bright music) So this is the chain of command used to launch nuclear strikes in the US. But there is one big
problem with this logic, because all of this only works effectively if the US launches the initial strike. But what if another nation
strikes the US first instead? A nuclear detonation releases a wave of electromagnetic pulses, or EMPs, and such a blast can take
out the electrical grid as well as any vulnerable
communication methods. This means that the
call from the president might not reach its designated target. Additionally, important command centers such as the Pentagon, the White House, or even Offutt Air Force
Base itself might be targets during a nuclear attack
and could be taken out. Therefore, the US wanted to prove that even if they are hit first, even if American cities, military bases and command structure is wiped out, they can still strike back. This idea became known as
mutually assured destruction. If any country does
attack the United States, the US will be able to retaliate. And so Operation Looking
Glass was established. This is the name for a series of aircraft, specifically EC-135s, that are designed to take over nuclear command authority should anything happen to
ground control at Offutt. Its name comes from its mission. It is meant to mirror or be a Looking Glass for ground control. And so Boeing KC-135
Stratotankers were stripped and retrofitted with
communications equipment to make sure they have the
same capabilities in the air as they would on the ground. But planes that are parked on
the ground are easy targets. And so beginning in 1961,
Operation Looking Glass goes on 24/7 airborne alert. (energetic music) This means that at least one of these aircraft is in the
air at any given moment. This way, even if the
entire Looking Glass fleet is destroyed, there will still
always be at least one EC-135 in the air that can take
over nuclear command. (bright music) What is almost unbelievable to me is that this airborne alert lasted for a staggering 29
years, from 1961 to 1990. For any given moment, day
or night, of those 29 years of US history, there always
was at least one EC-135 in the air ready to
launch a nuclear strike. Only in 1990, just as the
Cold War was cooling down, the constant airborne alert was halted. But even then, there's still
always at least one plane that remains ready to
take off within minutes. Eventually in the 1970s, these
EC-135 aircraft were replaced by a more modern Boeing
747-200s, retrofitted with all of the communications equipment needed to keep the president connected
to anywhere in the world. And these Boeing 747s make
up the Doomsday Plane fleet that is still being used to this day. So let's take a look inside to see what makes this such a unique aircraft. (bright music) Towards the very front of the plane, there is a command office suite, basically a private area
reserved for any VIP that may be traveling on the plane. This is likely where the
president will take up quarters should doomsday ever come, but in practice, it is
actually most commonly used by the Secretary of Defense, because while traveling abroad, the Secretary of Defense
typically flies using one of these aircraft. Just behind this suite is the galley, or the flight attendant station. And next to the galley is
a small conference room where meetings can be held in flight, almost like a flying situation room. It seats up to nine people and
could very well be the room where the fate of an
entire nation may be held if the United States
ever enters nuclear war. Just beyond the conference
room is a briefing area. Here, a podium is set up
so that leadership members can address their staff. There are also multiple
phones, as maintaining contact with military units, government agencies and command centers
around the world is one of the aircraft's primary missions. And during foreign visits,
this area also doubles as a press room where
journalists can be seated and press conferences
can be held mid-flight. (bright music) Continuing on past this room
is the Battle Staff Area. This is the largest room inside the plane. Here, several workstations are set up, and you'll find equipment you'd expect to se in a typical office
setting, like computers, phones, printers and copiers. It is essentially a cubicle space. From here, the military staff
can track unfolding events and can help coordinate a
response to a national emergency. Just past the Battle Staff Area is the communication section. This is where the aircraft
communication specialists work to maintain contact with
different military units. The aircraft is equipped with multiple redundant
communication systems, and if one network becomes unavailable, operators can quickly identify the issue and switch to another system. (bright music) Also monitored from here is the aircraft's survivable
super high frequency, or SHF system. This system is located in
the distinctive hump on top of the aircraft, and inside
it, there is an antenna that transmits very short radio waves capable of carrying large amounts of information across long distances. This system is primarily used
to establish direct links with US military satellites in orbit, providing a highly secure means of communication even when
other networks are unavailable. (bright music) And just below the
communications workstation sits probably the most complex piece of communications
equipment on this aircraft. In the middle of this room
sits a compartment containing a spool of antenna cable. This cable can be deployed
while the aircraft is in flight. Then the wire is reeled out
through the back of the plane and it is trailing behind
it through the sky. At full length, this antenna extends a staggering five miles. (bright music) This enormous length is needed to create a very low frequency antenna. Very low frequency radio
wavelengths are absolutely massive, stretching for miles, and to
transmit them effectively, you need an antenna that is at least some meaningful fraction of that wavelength. When this antenna is in use, the aircraft typically flies
in gentle banking turns, which helps to keep the wire stable and hanging in a more controlled
position behind the plane. Basically, the jet has to
carefully fly in circles while dragging the cable
behind and below it. (bright music) The benefit of transmitting
at these frequencies is that they can travel
incredibly long distances, and more importantly, they can
partially penetrate seawater, which means this aircraft
can communicate with one of the most critical parts
of America's nuclear arsenal, ballistic missile submarines, (video whooshes) hiding below the ocean. (bright music) Two operators can sit
at the station to deploy and monitor the antenna, and
a periscope lets them see the cable while it is trailing behind. These operators can then
communicate with the pilots to ensure that they
are flying the aircraft at the right speed and height to make sure turbulence
doesn't damage the antenna. (bright music) Located just above this
room is a small section with additional seating as
well as the crew rest area. The Doomsday Plane is capable
of mid-flight refueling and is designed to stay in the air for extended periods of time. If necessary, the plane
can stay in the air for an entire week without
ever needing to ground. By that point, the aircraft
could have theoretically circled the earth more than four times
all without a single stop. The only reason the plane
would need to land after a week is because the engines
would run out of lubricant. (bright music) And just in case this rest
area isn't enough space, there is an additional
one upstairs as well just behind the cockpit. One thing that sets this plane apart from other Boeing 747s is that many of the airplane systems
have been specially hardened to ensure that they can survive
the electromagnetic blast released during a nuclear strike. The plane's windows are
covered in wire mesh that helps prevent powerful
electromagnetic pulses from damaging sensitive systems. And even in a time of
modern glass cockpits, most of the controls in this
plane remain analog, another precaution to
protect the Doomsday Plane from a potential EMP blast that could disrupt sensitive
electronic equipment. (bright music) Everything about the
Doomsday Plane is set up to support the President
and Secretary of Defense if the day of nuclear war ever comes. It is an essential aspect of deterrence for the United States, and
these are just the E-4B, of which there are four aircraft. These are operated by the US Air Force. (bright music) In addition, there are also
16 E-6 Mercury Aircraft that are operated by the US Navy with somewhat overlapping
responsibilities. Together, these aircraft create
a highly redundant command and control network. If critical infrastructure
on the ground is damaged or destroyed, many of the
same functions can be shifted into the air, helping ensure that orders can still be transmitted and received during a national emergency. (bright music) To me, the airborne lake
of the Triad remains one of the most fascinating
elements of military technology, and no aircraft embodies this
better than the B-2 Spirit, a bomber so advanced that
more than three decades after its first flight, it
still looks like something from the future. Capable, of flying at
high subsonic speeds, the bomber can be anywhere in the world in less than half a day. (bright music) My friends over at Mustard have made an incredible documentary covering how the B-2 was developed, and they are using incredibly
detailed 3D animations to visualize what makes it
such a remarkable aircraft. They also just recently
started a brand new series called "Unsealed", where each
episode takes a deep dive into the design process behind some of history's most ambitious
engineering projects. (bright music) For example, the second episode of this series explores
the chain of compromises and cost-cutting measures that
ultimately led to the crash of a DC-10 in 1979. "Unsealed" is available to
watch exclusively on Nebula, which is also where I
have released several of my own exclusive documentaries. So many creators you
probably already watch are making bigger and more
ambitious projects on Nebula. There are comedy series
like "Abolish Everything", history documentaries like
"The Battle of Britain", as well as short and feature length films. Basically, I'm listing all this to say that Nebula has way more
than just airplane videos, but if you are interested
(bright music) in planes, we do tend to have a pretty good
selection of that as well. If you sign up using the link below or scan the QR code on the
screen, you will get 50% of an annual subscription
so you can enjoy Nebula for just $2.50 a month. (bright music continues) Thanks for the support,
and thank you so much for watching this video. (bright music continues)
